first_turn_cross_session_reuse.scope: Full reusable boundary on each session's first turn, which has no previous request in that session: observed reuse is cross-session. This does not exhaust shared reuse on later turns. Primary within-session return eligibility is unchanged.

holds.scope: Observed owner/generation lifetimes; snapshots bound appearance/disappearance and do not establish exact release or expiry times. Final-turn holds have no later recorded return, including truncated ends. return_release is an observation/attempt counter, not a count of held leases released. Metadata-only mutations can be missed by snapshot deduplication.

refusal_scope: Instantaneous native capacity replay ignores holds and excludes in-flight/protected offered keys. No direct obstruction does not rule out indirect cache/scheduling effects; paired refusal counts remain outcomes. Frozen screen has no store-frequency admission threshold.

resource_details.scope: Observed process-counter deltas by PID/start identity; startup includes loading/staging. First samples can miss early faults, vanished processes can be missed, RSS double-counts shared pages, GPU values include graphics and are sample means rather than time integrals. GPU clocks and Windows process activity were not captured.

resources.limits: sampled Linux process counters; partial edge intervals prorated; processes that start and exit between samples and Windows activity can be missed; memory/swap cover startup through the final pre-cleanup sample

scope: Derived diagnostics, preserving primary metrics and raw records. Latency descriptions are unweighted and complete-response-only, with all failure denominators alongside them; inferential comparisons use the frozen post-stratified estimator.

working_set.definition: current submitted prompt's largest reusable native boundary, window/recurrent reachable keys, unique physical-key union while session active; no future turns, independent of cache readiness
